newsitem.title: ISRAEL: NBA star keeps promise to meet Israeli rabbi.
newsitem.headline: NBA star keeps promise to meet Israeli rabbi.

text.p: Former U.S. basketball star Kareem Abdul-Jabbar had a tall order when he arrived in Israel on Thursday -- to meet the Jewish state's chief rabbi.
Abdul-Jabbar said a black family friend was among the U.S. soldiers who liberated the Nazi concentration camp where Rabbi Yisrael Meir Lau was the youngest survivor at the end of World War Two.
The friend, Leonard Smith from Queens, New York, was unable to make the trip himself but urged Abdul-Jabbar to meet the rabbi.
Rabbi Lau, who was seven when he was liberated, said he remembered black soldiers among the liberators, adding: "The first black face I saw in my life was in the broken gates of Buchenwald".
Lau said he hoped Jewish-black relationships in the United States, now tense, would improve. "It's time to forget all the differences and hold our hands together," he said.
Abdul-Jabbar urged Lau not to forget black America's role in World War Two. "It's not in the history books. It's fading from sight," said Abdul-Jabbar, in Israel for a streetball tournament.
Abdul-Jabbar, who is 7-feet 2-inches tall, retired from professional basketball in 1989 after 20 seasons and with six NBA championships under his belt.
Born Lew Alcindor, he converted to Islam while in the NBA. He said he would pray at a mosque on Temple Mount on Friday.
